findings.summary: Generic helper function names that don't communicate intent
evidence: parsePathUUID, parsePagination, parseDateParam - generic names that don't indicate domain context
cloneJSONB, stringifyInstanceID - utility functions without clear domain purpose
messageMetadataBool, isPlaceholderMessageBody - names are descriptive but inconsistent with other helpers
findings.suggestion: Rename helpers to indicate their domain context (e.g., parseUUIDFromPath, parsePaginationParams, parseDateQueryParam). Group related helpers by domain (contact helpers, message helpers, etc.)

findings.summary: Inconsistent naming between resolve/load/get prefixes
evidence: getChatbotSettingsCached vs resolveTemplateAgentName vs loadChatCloseRatingSettings
Mixed use of get, load, resolve, find prefixes without clear distinction
getChatbotFlowsCached, getChatbotFlowByIDCached - 'Cached' suffix only on some functions
findings.suggestion: Establish naming convention: 'get' for simple retrieval, 'load' for database queries, 'resolve' for computed/derived values, 'find' for searches. Add 'Cached' suffix consistently to all cached accessors

findings.summary: Inconsistent abbreviations (org, ctx, req, resp)
evidence: orgID, userID, ctx, req, resp used inconsistently
Some functions use full 'organization', others use 'org'
msg vs message inconsistency (SendOutgoingMessage vs msgReq)
findings.suggestion: Establish standard abbreviations: org (organization), ctx (context), req (request), resp (response). Use consistently or document exceptions. Prefer full names in public APIs

findings.summary: Dead code paths after unconditional returns
evidence: Lines 220-223: parseDateRange error handling falls back to default but the error is ignored
Lines 269-274: Duplicate fallback logic in GetAgentComparison - same pattern as GetAgentDetails
Error result from parseDateRange stored but never used before falling back to default
findings.suggestion: Either return the error to the caller or remove the error path entirely. If fallback is intentional, add explanatory comment. Consider extracting date parsing logic to avoid duplication

findings.summary: Redundant nil checks on values that cannot be nil
evidence: Line 134: resolveTemplateAgentName checks 'a == nil || a.DB == nil' - but this is called on method receiver 'a' which cannot be nil in normal Go usage
Line 145: resolveTemplateOrganizationName has similar redundant 'a == nil' checks
Line 228: scheduleContactAvatarRefresh checks 'a == nil' unnecessarily
findings.suggestion: Remove nil checks on method receivers. If defensive programming is needed, use assertions or document preconditions. Consider making these free functions if nil checks are truly needed

findings.summary: Deeply nested conditional logic that's hard to follow
evidence: Lines 238-276: readChatCloseRatingFollowupState has 4 levels of nested type switches and conditionals
Lines 650-685: parseInboundRatingValue has complex rune-by-rune parsing with nested loops and conditionals
Lines 901-936: extractFollowupCommentsForRatingMessage deeply nested type assertions
findings.suggestion: Extract nested logic into separate functions with clear names. Use early returns to reduce nesting. Consider strategy pattern for type handling

findings.summary: Identical or very similar code in multiple branches
evidence: Lines 546-550: IsSelf check logic duplicated with slight variations
Lines 518-538: parseStatusFont has duplicate error handling patterns
Multiple places have identical error logging patterns
findings.suggestion: Extract common logic to helper functions. Create shared error handling helpers. Use table-driven approaches for repetitive validation

findings.summary: Type assertions on JSONB values without checking ok return
evidence: Line 281: status.Metadata["from_me"].(bool) - only checks ok, ignores false case
Lines 423-437: Multiple type assertions on JSONB with inconsistent ok checking
Line 132: messageMetadataBool does check ok but many other places don't follow this pattern
findings.suggestion: Always check both return values from type assertions. Create helper functions for common JSONB access patterns. Consider using a typesafe wrapper for JSONB

findings.summary: Excessive use of 'any' type loses type safety
evidence: Line 31: Metadata any in ContactResponse - could be structured type
Line 59: Content any in MessageResponse - loses content type information
chat_close_ratings.go: Entries []any in chatCloseRatingFollowupState
findings.suggestion: Define specific types for metadata (e.g., type-safe structs with JSON tags). Use union types or interfaces for Content instead of any. Document the expected structure when any is necessary

findings.summary: Inconsistent UUID handling between string and uuid.UUID types
evidence: stringifyInstanceID converts uuid.UUID to *string but many places need manual string() conversion
InstanceID *string in ContactResponse but should be *uuid.UUID or consistently string
parsePathUUID returns uuid.UUID but many callers immediately call .String()
findings.suggestion: Standardize on uuid.UUID in internal code, convert to string only at API boundaries. Use consistent pointer vs value semantics (prefer value for UUID)

findings.summary: Functions return error without specifying expected error types
evidence: DownloadAndSaveMedia returns error but doesn't document what errors it can return
getChatbotSettingsCached returns error but callers don't distinguish between cache miss, db error, or decrypt error
No custom error types for common failure modes
findings.suggestion: Define custom error types for expected failure modes. Use error wrapping with fmt.Errorf. Document in comments what errors can be returned

findings.summary: Functions perform side effects not indicated by name
evidence: getChatbotSettingsCached: 'get' suggests pure read but it decrypts keys and mutates the settings object
resolveTemplateAgentName: 'resolve' suggests pure function but may update cache
handleManualChatCloseRatingPrompt: sends messages, creates DB records - too much for 'handle'
findings.suggestion: Rename functions to reflect all side effects (e.g., getAndDecryptChatbotSettings, sendAndStoreCloseRatingPrompt). Split functions if they do multiple unrelated things

findings.summary: Functions don't clearly document what they return on error
evidence: findByIDAndOrg: returns error but also sends HTTP response - unclear contract
parsePathUUID: sends error envelope before returning - caller must return nil but this isn't documented
parsePagination: no error case but silently clamps values - unclear if this is intentional
findings.suggestion: Separate validation from response sending. Use sentinel error pattern consistently. Document behavior when input is invalid (clamp vs error vs default)

findings.summary: Functions in same module have different error handling contracts
evidence: Some functions return error and send response (Login), others only send response (CreateAccount)
Inconsistent use of errEnvelopeSent pattern - some check for it, others don't
Mixed use of returning nil vs returning error after sending response
findings.suggestion: Establish standard error handling contract: either always return error OR always send response and return nil. Don't mix patterns in same module

findings.summary: Functions handle nil pointer parameters inconsistently
evidence: Some functions treat nil instanceID as 'filter all', others as error
resolveTemplateAgentName checks for nil contact but other template functions don't
Inconsistent nil handling for *uuid.UUID parameters across codebase
findings.suggestion: Document nil parameter handling in function comments. Use consistent pattern (nil = unfiltered, nil = error, or nil = use default). Consider using functional options pattern for multiple optional params

findings.summary: Inconsistent error handling across modules
evidence: Some functions return errors (cache.go), others send HTTP responses (helpers.go), some log and continue
errEnvelopeSent pattern used in some places but not others
Media functions wrap errors with fmt.Errorf but cache functions return raw errors
findings.suggestion: Choose one error strategy per layer (handlers send responses, services return errors). Use consistent error wrapping. Document error handling strategy for each layer

findings.summary: Errors caught and re-thrown without wrapping original context
evidence: Line 104: decryptChatbotAIKey wraps error but original crypto error context is in message
Line 579: resolveClosePromptAccount returns generic error when multiple things can fail
Many places: errors from DB queries returned directly without adding context about what was being queried
findings.suggestion: Always wrap errors with context using fmt.Errorf or errors.Wrap. Include what operation failed, not just that it failed. Use structured logging with original error

findings.summary: Errors logged but not propagated or recovered from
evidence: Line 301: Failed to update status seen timestamp - logged but operation continues
Line 276: Failed to persist resolved channel name - logged but function continues
Line 447: cache unmarshal errors ignored and treated as cache miss
findings.suggestion: Either propagate the error or explicitly document why it's safe to ignore. For cache, consider corrupted data eviction. For DB updates, consider retry or user notification

findings.summary: Mix of string errors, sentinel errors, and custom error types
evidence: errEnvelopeSent is sentinel error but only used in helpers
String literals used for errors throughout ("Invalid credentials", "Failed to...")
crypto.ErrMissingEncryptionKey is custom error type but other crypto errors are strings
No custom error types for domain-specific failures (auth, validation, etc.)
findings.suggestion: Define custom error types for domain errors. Use sentinel errors for control flow (validation failures). Use string errors only for user-facing messages. Document error type hierarchy

findings.summary: I/O operations without proper error handling
evidence: Line 193: os.WriteFile error wrapped but doesn't handle disk full or permission errors
Line 29: os.MkdirAll error returned but caller doesn't check for specific failures
Line 480: io.ReadAll error handling doesn't distinguish between timeout vs EOF
findings.suggestion: Check for specific I/O error types (os.ErrPermission, os.ErrExist). Handle disk space errors explicitly. Add context about what file/path was being accessed
